tagline: Country roads around a depot town, and a working mill.
intro: In southwestern Fairfax County the byways are a knot of country roads around Clifton, Popes Head and Yates Ford, Henderson and Newman, Compton and Fairfax Station. The land stays thinly built. When development crept close in the late 1970s and early 1980s, an ordinance allowed one building to an undivided five acres, to spare the Occoquan Reservoir, and the woods and horse country stayed.
Farther north, Hunter Mill Road runs up from Oakton, and Colvin Run Road follows an old line of Route 7 past a mill.

moments.title: Clifton
moments.text: The village grew up around Clifton Station, a depot opened in 1868, and with 243 people in 2020 it is the smallest of Fairfax County's three towns by a wide margin.

moments.title: Fairfax Station
moments.text: In August 1862 Clara Barton tended the wounded of Second Bull Run at this railroad station, and the depot museum is a replica of the station built in 1891.

moments.title: Colvin Run Mill
moments.text: Addison Millard bought the mill in 1883 and moved into the miller's house with his wife Emma and some of their 20 children; it is the area's last working water-powered mill of its century.
